opener_concept: A class of 24 students' lunch choices drawn as a real pie chart (SVG): half the circle is chips. Box 1 asks how many students chose chips (12, pure common sense from 'half of 24'), box 2 asks how many degrees of turn that half takes (180). The reveal names it: a pie chart turns a share of a group into a share of one full turn, readable forwards to an angle or backwards to a number of people, and a histogram does the same job for grouped measurements where the size of the bar, not its label, carries the number.
